03 / THE COUPLED BICYCLE

One bike. Two contact patches.

See how fork, frame and rear suspension share a bump. Compare hardtail and full suspension, then let a passive rider mass move with the bike.

Bike & excitation

SI UNITS
Rider mass and compliance

Lower stops push the rider up; upper stops push down. Ultimate travel still terminates unsupported runs.

The rider share leaves at least 5 kg in the frame. Compression is positive down the frame guide; extension is negative. These values describe a synthetic spring, not human anatomy.

Fork buffer properties

Illustrative compliant buffers inside the 160 mm stroke. Spring force grows quadratically; damping acts only while entering the buffer. Ultimate travel still stops unsupported runs.

Linkage geometry & presets

Frame coordinates: x forward, z up; BB = (0, −0.315) m. Arm-eye coordinates are relative to the main pivot at zero swing. Changing a point changes the solver and drawing together.

Annotated eyes follow the reviewed photograph and 210 × 55 mm shock specification. Pivot placement, frame proportions and masses remain estimates, not a calibrated production bike.

Shock buffer properties

Inside the configured shock stroke. Forces act through changing single-pivot leverage; no additional wheel spring. Dormant on a hardtail.

Tyre and calculation settings

Total includes frame and rider; passive mode splits it into two bodies. Front assembly 3 kg; rear assembly 4 kg. All parameters are illustrative, with no real-bike calibration.

Attachment loads

RECORDED ENDPOINTS

World +x forward, +z up, +My nose-down. Parent-on-child reactions: rider guide at rider COM; fixture at frame origin; rear bearing at main pivot (hardtail: rigid axle attachment). Rider loads describe one guide, not hands, feet or saddle. Equal-and-opposite reactions must be compared at the same point. These are not breaking-force thresholds.

Experiment record

Waiting for calculation.

Two flat, prescribed platens; linear suspension and vertical tyre surrogate. The passive rider is one guided mass; no separate hand, foot or saddle contact. Optional fork and shock buffers model finite compliance, not rigid impacts or component survival. Rider stops add finite compliance; ultimate travel remains enforced. No steering, rolling/slip or terrain layers. Ultimate travel still stops the run. Unloaded frame+rider inertia is 8 kg·m², split by mass in passive mode; gravity sag then moves the rider COM. No anatomical calibration.
